item.title: Game time set for No. 19 Texas vs. Mississippi State
item.description: STARKVILLE, MISSISSIPPI - OCTOBER 25: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns carries the ball during the first half against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium on October 25, 2025 in Starkville, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The third straight home game for the No. 19 Texas Longhorns will kick off at 6:30 p.m. Central on ABC or ESPN as Steve Sarkisian’s team hosts the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 31. Before Mississippi State arrives on the Forty Acres for the second time as an SEC opponent, Sarkisian hopes to end his team’s losing streak with a matchup against No. 7 Ole Miss on Saturday. Texas is currently 4-2 after back-to-back losses to unranked opponents by matching 27-24 scores. The Longhorns opened as 3.5-point favorites over the Rebels on Sunday, according to FanDuel . Like Texas, Mississippi State got off to a 4-0 start, rising to No. 16 in the AP Top 25, before dropping consecutive games. For head coach Jeff Lebby, those losses happened in blowout fashion — 56-23 to then-No. 7 Alabama and 31-0 to then-No. 22 LSU. Mississippi State hosts Oklahoma in Starkville this weekend.

item.title: Colin Simmons injury update: Texas edge rusher expected to miss multiple weeks
item.description: Trainers check on Texas edge Colin Simmons (1) after an injury during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football paired the insult of a second straight SEC loss with a critical injury Saturday afternoon, one that will reportedly keep its best defensive player off the field through October Longhorns edge rusher Colin Simmons is expected to miss three-to-four weeks with a high ankle sprain, according to OrangeBloods' Anwar Richardson . Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian declined to address reports of Simmons' expected absence Monday. Simmons' status for Week 8 against Ole Miss will first be officially shared by Texas in Wednesday's injury report. I was told that Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons is expected to miss three to four weeks with a high ankle sprain. Simmons underwent an MRI on Monday that revealed no structural damage. The goal is to get him healthy and back on the field as soon as possible. In addition, I was told that running back Hollywood Smothers is dealing with an undisclosed injury, and his status for Saturday's game against Ole Miss is questionable. https://t.co/s2ZhKHJTKj - Anwar Richardson (@AnwarRichardson) October 19, 2026 Simmons exited Texas' 27-24 loss to Florida early in the fourth quarter. He engaged with a Florida offensive lineman on a running play, then crumpled to the ground as the play came to its conclusion. Simmons remained on the turf for more than a minute as he grabbed his right knee and ankle, and he was helped off the field by Texas staff. Simmons then went to Texas' locker room and did not log another snap. Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian said after the game he did not know the extent of Simmons' injury. Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Simmons' expected absence halts one of the more impressive defensive seasons in Texas history. Simmons' 10½ sacks through six games places him No. 7 on the Longhorns' all-time single-season sacks list. Simmons also is now up to 31½ career sacks, which is No. 3 in Texas history behind Tim Campbell (1979-80) and Kiki DeAyala (1980-82). Target acquired https://t.co/ly5wPlG2wy - Texas Football (@TexasFootball) October 17, 2026 Simmons is perhaps college football's premier pass rusher. He's the undisputed engine of Texas' defense. He's now on the mend through at least October, bringing a major blow to a Longhorns' defense now reeling after back-to-back losses. Q of the week: Best coach of all time? item.title: Rematch? UFC fighter who choked out Darren Till just signed with BKFC
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 04: (L-R) Derek Brunson elbows Darren Till of England in their middleweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at UFC APEX on September 04, 2021 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Darren Till may get an opportunity to avenge his submission loss to Derek Brunson at UFC Vegas 36 . That’s because Brunson, 42, recently signed a multi-fight deal with Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) and will make his in-ring debut at the upcoming BKFC “Fight Night” event on Fri., Nov. 20, 2026 inside Myrtle Beach Sports Center in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. “I’m excited to compete again,” Brunson said. “I’ve been training for the past three years, getting my younger guys ready. Time to get back out there and have some fun. I have a very strong grind in me right now.” Brunson has not competed since losing to Rodolfo Vieira at ADXC 7 back in late 2024. “We’re honored to have Derek Brunson sign with BKFC,” said David Feldman, Founder and President of BKFC. “We’ve long admired his world class skills and can’t wait to see him in the Squared Circle. We’re positive he’s going to make some serious noise fighting for BKFC.” The 33-year-old Till, who joined BKFC back in April , has yet to comment on the addition of his former foe.

item.title: Rays, Guardians Offenses May Already Be Doomed Against Brewers
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher JoJo Romero The Milwaukee Brewers will play either the Cleveland Guardians or the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, but regardless of who they play, their southpaws will be at a huge advantage. The Brewers dominated the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, and a lot of the credit goes to the pitching staff. Specifically, the Brewers' array of elite left-handed pitchers has dominated in the postseason. On a pitching staff that features Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson, it's been the bullpen and Robert Gasser that have been the biggest story. Gasser has had the two best starts by Brewers starting pitchers this postseason, and left-handers Aaron Ashby, JoJo Romero and DL Hall have been phenomenal. How good have they been? Well, the Dodgers had the sixth-best wRC+ and the fifth-best OPS against left-handed pitching. The Brewers' group of Gasser, Ashby, Romero and Hall combined to allow just seven hits in 17 2/3 innings. They struck out 13 batters as well. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The Guardians ranked 25th in wRC+ against lefties and 27th in OPS against left-handed pitching in the regular season. The Rays ranked 26th in wRC+ and 25th in OPS. If the Dodgers couldn't crack the code against the Brewers' lefties, the Guardians and Rays might be doomed. The Rays have been better against lefties in the postseason, but the Guardians' struggles have continued. The Brewers have relied on their bullpen a ton during this run, and their group of lefties combined with power right-handers like Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe and Jacob Misiorowski make them a tough team to face. item.title: Inside the ‘MNF’ Booth Blowup: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman Nearly Had Physical Altercation
item.description: BILL GREENBLATT/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency; John Fycke/AdMedia/Newscom/The Mega Agency Joe Buck and Troy Aikman , who have covered football together for nearly 25 years, were seen in a tense moment ahead of the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium in LA — and the Monday Night Football game on October 12 came close to getting violent in the broadcast booth, a source tells In Touch . “It nearly got physical off air,” the source tells In Touch exclusively. “They were very close from coming to blows.” The source reveals the conflict stems from the deal Buck, 57, recently made to renew his ESPN contract — which The Athletic reported is for six years and $108 million last month — without telling Aikman, 59. “Joe signed his new deal and never said a word to Troy. Not one word,” adds the source. “They’ve been partners for more than 20 years. In this business, when something like that is happening, the bosses and your partner sit you down and tell you. That’s standard practice. Nobody did that for Troy.” “People who’ve worked closely with both of them say they’ve never seen a betrayal like it,” the source continues. “It’s the biggest betrayal anyone in the industry can remember.” ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback told KTCK radio station on October 15 that he would soon be “a free agent,” according to The Athletic , and appeared to address his partner’s decision. “There’s probably a time and a place for all that to be discussed,” Aikman said. “I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know that it’s hard to figure out kind of what’s happened.” The source tells In Touch their relationship has been destroyed. “There’s real hatred between them now. It’s never been this toxic,” says the source. “They were closer than friends. They were like brothers.” And the pair will still be forced to call Super Bowl LXI together in February, the source points out. “Troy has to sit there, smile and do his job like the pro he is until it’s over.” Read More From InTouch Weekly ‘Full House’ Star Jodie Sweetin Recalls Bob Saget Helping Her Escape Drive-By Shooting ‘Teen Mom’ Stars Catelynn and Tyler Baltierra’s Daughter, 11, Pens ‘Powerful’ Poem About Cornell 7's Jane Doe Miley Cyrus Claims Dolly Parton Communicates With Her Post-Death This story Inside the ‘MNF’ Booth Blowup: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman Nearly Had Physical Altercation first appeared on InTouch Weekly . item.title: Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie set for Glasgow debut
item.description: Ritchie spent 11 years with Glasgow's rivals Edinburgh after joining straight from school [SNS] Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut. The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been sidelined for the opening months of the season because of ankle and Achilles tendon issues. The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, is now back in full training and is expected to play in Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) match against Benetton in Treviso. "He's training fully. We feel he's integrated into the systems now very well. And he's itching to go," said Carolan. "It would be great if we get him involved this week, either starting or on the bench. It would be really positive to have him involved, especially ahead of Scotland's Nations Cup in a couple of weeks." Ritchie was a pillar of the Edinburgh team for more than a decade before moving to the French Top 14 side. Carolan believes patience will pay off for the Warriors with Ritchie, who has moved to Scotstoun on a two-year deal. "I think it was important to get the timing right. We didn't want to rush him," the Irishman added. "Obviously he had surgery over the summer so we didn't really want to push him. He's just moved to a new club and with all that going on, we felt the timing needed to be right. "We could have involved him maybe last week but that was Ruwald van der Merwe's time. So I think the time has now come to unleash Jamie Ritchie in a Glasgow Warriors shirt." Warriors are second in the URC table after three matches - behind Edinburgh - and will be favourite against second-bottom Benetton this weekend. They finished top of the URC last season but were knocked out of the play-offs in the semi-finals by the Bulls and the arrivals of Ritchie and Van der Merwe - with Scotland back row Jack Dempsey departing - were part of an evolution of Franco Smith's squad in the summer. item.title: Yaya Touré: ‘Slovan come to Roma to win, Gasperini was incredible at Atalanta’
item.description: Yaya Touré: ‘Slovan come to Roma to win, Gasperini was incredible at Atalanta’ Slovan Bratislava coach Yaya Touré insists his side are heading to Roma to win, while hailing Gian Piero Gasperini’s work at Atalanta as “incredible”. With quotes courtesy of TuttoMercatoWeb , the former Manchester City midfielder spoke at his press conference ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash at the Stadio Olimpico. “I believe you always keep learning. He has great experience and made an enormous contribution at Atalanta, improving every aspect of their game. The work he did there was incredible,” he said. Touré took charge in June in his first job as a head coach, having previously been Roberto Mancini’s assistant with Saudi Arabia. He guided Slovan into the league phase with an extra-time win over Celje in the play-off, but they have lost both games so far, 6-1 at Paris Saint-Germain and 3-0 at home to Stuttgart. ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 14: Donyell Malen and Niccolo Pisilli of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammates during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AS Roma and Real Madrid C.F. at Stadio Olimpico on October 14, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Touré: ‘Roma can hurt you a lot’ Roma are without Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné, Bryan Cristante and Mile Svilar, and have one point from two games after the 4-3 defeat to Real Madrid . “For me it’s very complicated, but I want to keep things simple,” Touré explained. “We’re up against a very strong team. They have some absences, but they’re still strong and they can hurt you a lot. I’m focusing on my team.” Slovan have caused Roma problems before. They knocked the Giallorossi out of the Europa League play-off round in 2011, winning 1-0 in Bratislava and drawing 1-1 in Rome. “We’re here to win. Then it depends on what we do on the pitch, and we have to give the best performance possible,” Touré said. “We learned a lot from the last two games, and now we want to show our character without fear.” “Football is about enjoying the game and giving our fans something to be happy about. Then, if we lose, so be it.”

What we got was a jumbled up mess, with the 3-4-2-1 unable to provide the necessary creativity in attack to muster up anything to challenge Mandas in goal, who may have had the easiest game against Juve in his career tonight. It’s early, which is the saving grace for this, but Spalletti needs to fix this, and he needs to do it fast. item.title: O'Sullivan loses to Cheung in NI Open return
item.description: O'Sullivan was playing in the NI Open for the first time since 2022 [Getty Images] Ronnie O'Sullivan's poor form continued as the seven-time world champion was beaten 4-3 by world-ranked 110 player Ka Wai Cheung in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast After a strong start from Cheung, the three-time runner-up won three frames in a row before a valiant comeback from the Hong Kong player knocked out the 50-year-old. Cheung will now face the winner of Stuart Bingham and Yao Pengcheng's match for a spot in the last 16. O'Sullivan is now the eighth top 16 player to lose of the nine who have played at the Waterfront Hall so far. Mark Selby, Neil Robertson, Xiao Guodong, Shaun Murphy and Ali Carter fell on Sunday, with Chris Wakelin, Barry Hawkins and O'Sullivan following them out of the tournament on Monday. O'Sullivan had not played at a tournament in the United Kingdom since April's World Championship loss to John Higgins and it was not the victorious return he would have hoped for. The world number 13 was making a first appearance at the NI Open since 2022 and was playing in a Home Nations event for the first time since the 2024 English Open. Cheung made a bright start and claimed the opening frame but O'Sullivan responded to that early setback by claiming the next three frames in speedy and emphatic fashion. Breaks of 56,138 and 72 saw him move 3-1 ahead but that was as good as it got for the three-time NI Open finalist. Just as it looked like O'Sullivan had found form, he missed a good chance on a red in the fifth and Cheung clinched the frame after a run of 88. Cheung's confidence grew and he forced a deciding frame with another impressive 77. Another costly miss from O'Sullivan gave the 27-year-old the chance to advance which he did with a break of 61. "I'm very happy that I can still play well under pressure," reflected Cheung when he spoke to BBC Sport NI after the match. "To be honest, as you can see in the arena, Ronnie had a lot of fans. I was actually scared a little bit before the match but this is the best experience. "No matter if I had lost or won, I think it is the best experience for my snooker career and that is all I need. "To play the legend of the game and to win, this is very satisfying for me." In Monday's other afternoon games, Hawkins was beaten 4-2 by Daniel Wells but former world champion and 2024 NI Open champion Kyren Wilson progressed to round two with a comfortable 4-0 win over Ben Mertens. Wakelin lost 4-1 to Welshman Jamie Jones earlier in the day, while Luca Brecel got the better of Lei Peifan by the same scoreline. World number three Judd Trump and Scot John Higgins are among those in action during the evening session that begins at 19.00 BST.

item.description: KNOXVILLE, TN - OCTOBER 17: Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) stands in the pocket under pressure from Tennessee Volunteers defensive lineman Tyree Weathersby (18) during the college football game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Alabama Crimson Tide on October 17, 2026, at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, TN. Naturally, there were plenty of standouts and heroes from the game. But on Monday, the SEC recognized two of them as players of the week at their respective positions: DL Ty Weathersby and K Cooper Ranvier. weekly @SEC honors Defensive Lineman OTW » Tyree Weathersby Special Teams POTW » Cooper Ranvier read more → https://t.co/ahz78MEwva #GBO 🍊 pic.twitter.com/c0PwsUth5Q — Tennessee Football (@Vol_Football) October 19, 2026 Weathersby earned lineman of the week honors with a disruptive day off the edge. Weathersby also picked up the fumble by Keelon Russell in the first quarter after Jeremiah Telander —who also had a terrific game with two sacks and a fourth down stop — sacked Russell, he and rumbled 20 yards for what appeared to be a touchdown. The play was called back because Weathersby’s knee was down, but it was still a fumble recovery that led to points. Those 12 points off of field goals were enough to outscore Alabama’s entire team on the day. item.description: ‘A completely different beast’: Suryakumar Yadav reveals Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma’s influence on his fitness and leadership originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Suryakumar Yadav took part in an interview with "Mashable Middle East," where he discussed various topics during a drive in the UAE. SKY recalled observing Virat Kohli’s training sessions after making his India debut in 2021, describing him as a "completely different beast". Suryakumar said he learnt leadership qualities from Rohit Sharma after playing alongside him at Mumbai Indians and under him for India. Suryakumar Yadav reveals what he learnt from Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma Suryakumar Yadav has revealed how Virat Kohli’s approach to fitness and Rohit Sharma’s leadership influenced him during his time alongside two of Indian cricket’s most prominent players. The former Indian captain was speaking to a popular TV host, Rannvijay Singha, on the 42nd episode of the "Dubai journey" on the "Mashable Middle East" YouTube channel. While Kohli made an impression on Suryakumar through his training standards, Rohit taught him valuable lessons about understanding teammates and building relationships within a team. Suryakumar made his India debut in 2021, when Kohli was the national team captain, explaining how he deliberately tried to learn from Kohli’s preparation. "He was a completely different beast, and still is," Suryakumar said. The India batter also spoke about what he picked up from Rohit, under whom he played at Mumbai Indians before spending several years together in international cricket. Suryakumar Yadav reveals how Virat Kohli influenced his fitness Suryakumar named Kohli when asked which Indian team player he looked up to for fitness and strength. The batter recalled hearing from other players about how Kohli carried himself during training sessions. However, seeing the former captain prepare in person gave him an opportunity to observe those standards closely. "When I made my debut for India in 2021, he was the captain. When I saw him for the first time during a practice session, I had only heard from other players how he carried himself during the session," Suryakumar said. “When he used to practise, when he used to train, I used to keep my training times with him to see what he was training. He was a completely different beast, and still is,” he added. As evidenced by his career, fitness has been one of SKY's standout traits, and the team's decision to place him in key positions on the field is proof of that. Of course, his catch in the 2024 T20 World Cup final against South Africa which turned the game in India's favour remains one of the best picks in cricket history. Suryakumar Yadav explains what he learnt from Rohit Sharma’s leadership While Kohli influenced Suryakumar’s understanding of fitness and training, Rohit’s biggest impact came through his leadership and ability to connect with teammates.

item.title: CFP Bracketology: Week 7
item.description: PROVO, UT - OCTOBER 17: Fans flood the field after the Brigham Young Cougars upset the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at LaVell Edwards Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Provo, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images With all the change happening in college football over the last five years, especially with NIL, the transfer portal, and ever-growing conferences, sometimes it feels like the sport has lost its magic. But it is important to remember that no matter how much money TV executives make or wealthy boosters throw at players for NIL, this is still a sport played by (mostly) 18-22 year olds. Chaos always finds a way. Five of the top seven ranked teams lost on Saturday to shake up the playoff picture. After Week 7, my projected field is as follows: P4 Champions: Miami, Ohio State, Georgia, BYU G6 Leader: James Madison At-Larges: Notre Dame, Indiana, Ole Miss, Texas Tech, UCLA, Utah, Tennessee Outside Looking In: Kentucky, Alabama, Houston, Iowa, USC Some notes from Week 7: I am torn between James Madison and Boise State as the G6 leader. JMU’s schedule is one of the weakest in the country, but Boise State has one loss already and is more likely to drop a second game than JMU is to lose once. Right now, I will put JMU in the spot, but if the Dukes lose a game, that is likely curtains for them with their weak schedule. The Big 12 is the biggest winner of the week. BYU, Utah, and Texas Tech all remain unbeaten, and Houston is still in the hunt with just one loss. The Holy War looms on November 7, and Utah will host Houston this Saturday. There is a strong possibility that the Big 12 gets multiple teams in the playoff. BYU has a signature win over Notre Dame on their resume that will be a safety net should the Cougars lose to someone other than Utah. The SEC has a logjam of teams around the bubble right now but it will not last because most of these teams have games remaining against each other. Texas and LSU are on life support and still have a game left against each other. Alabama has a decent chance of making the field if they win out, but they do not have any margin for error. Tennessee, Georgia, Ole Miss, and Kentucky are the only teams left in the conference with only one loss. UCLA and Texas Tech have favorable remaining schedules, although UCLA has lost its starting quarterback for the season. Bubble teams are hoping for a loss for either (or both) of them.

item.title: Of course Knicks’ OG Anunoby mentioned Anne Hathaway during Ben Stiller’s lie detector test hilarious in Focker-in-Law promo
item.description: Of course Knicks’ OG Anunoby mentioned Anne Hathaway during Ben Stiller’s lie detector test hilarious in Focker-in-Law promo appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ahead of the release of Focker-in-Law, the fourth movie in the Meet the Parents series, New York Knicks superfan Ben Stiller filmed a promotional video with star player OG Anunoby , who brought up his fan Anne Hathaway . The two linked up for the video , which features Stiller hooking Anunoby up to a lie detector test (Robert De Niro famously did the same to him in Meet the Parents). Immediately, Anunoby clocks Stiller, asking him if it was a promotion for his new movie. View this post on Instagram Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) To no one’s surprise, Anunoby wasn’t and doesn’t ever get “nervous.” He answers everything honestly, including declaring that he was a “better athlete” than Stiller. As the video unfolds, Stiller tries to catch Anunoby slipping. When asked for his “favorite actor,” Anunoby doesn’t hesitate before saying Hathaway’s name. When Stiller asks about his favorite “male actor,” he replies, “Will Ferrell.” Stiller finally thinks he has Anunoby where he wants him when he asks for his favorite scene from Meet the Parents. Naturally, Anunoby’s response is an embarrassing scene involving Stiller’s character. Towards the end, Stiller jokes that people sometimes call him “OG,” to which the Knicks forward replied, “Maybe because you’re old.” Once the test is over, Anunoby is ready to face Stiller one-on-one on the court. However, the Focker-in-Law star has to dart, leaving the Knicks player hooked up to the test. When asked if he can help him out, Stiller says, “No, I don’t even know how it works.” As he is left stranded, Anunoby calls Stiller back by several names, including “Ben,” “Benjamin,” and “Benji.” Suffice it to say, none of them work. Focker-in-Law is the fourth installment in the Meet the Parents series. Stiller, De Niro, Owen Wilson, Blythe Danner, and Teri Polo reprise their roles from previous movies. Some of the new members of the cast include Ariana Grande, Beanie Feldstein, and Skyler Gisondo. item.title: Josh Allen’s pressure-to-sack rate has gotten back to normal elite-level figure
item.description: The hidden superpower of Josh Allen is his ability to avoid sacks. He’s a magician who regularly conjures magnificent elusiveness inside and outside the pocket behind the line of scrimmage to make something out of what appears to be a dire situation. Allen getting extraordinarily good at evading sacks coincided with his ascension to elite status in the NFL. While the sharpening of that skill is certainly not the sole reason the Bills quarterback has been so good for so long now, the alignment of those timelines is both fascinating and telling. A season ago, when Allen took a career-high 40 sacks during the regular season, that superpower faded. The best way to quantifiably measure a quarterback’s elusiveness in the pocket is with the advanced metric pressure-to-sack rate, which is precisely what it sounds like — the frequency at which a quarterback pressure becomes a quarterback sack. For all intents and purposes, the line of demarcation for pressure-to-sack rate is 20% in the NFL. If a quarterback is near, at, or above a pressure-to-sack rate of 20%, he’s really struggling in this regard. If he’s closer to 15%, he’s doing fine work. If he’s hovering near 10% in pressure-to-sack rate, he’s probably the NFL’s most elusive quarterback in these scenarios. During the 40-sack 2025 campaign, Allen’s pressure-to-sack rate was 18.6%, his highest rate since 2019. It ranked 28th out of 45 qualifiers. Before that, here’s how Allen fared, by season, in this metric and where he ranked among qualifying quarterbacks (lower is better): 2024: 8.0% (1st/44) 2023: 10.3% (2nd/45) 2022: 14.7% (9th/41) 2021: 10.6% (1st/39) 2020: 10.7% (3rd/42) As you can see, I wasn’t exaggerating in the first few paragraphs. Allen has been a wizard in this area, and he’s been excellent avoiding sacks while pressured for a long time now. But many speculated the 18.6% pressure-to-sack rate during his Age 29 season in 2025 was the first sign of Allen’s decline. In the first three games of the 2026 campaign, he was sacked eight times and had pressure-to-sack rates of 16.7%, 11.8%, and a whopping 33.3% in the games leading into Week 4. I’ll give this next sentence a little Mark Twain twist — the reports of the death of Allen’s ability to evade sacks were greatly exaggerated. He’s a magician who regularly conjures magnificent elusiveness inside and outside the pocket behind the line of scrimmage to make something out of what appears to be a dire situation. Allen getting extraordinarily good at evading sacks coincided with his ascension to elite status in the NFL. While the sharpening of that skill is certainly not the sole reason the Bills quarterback has been so good for so long now, the alignment of those timelines is both fascinating and telling. A season ago, when Allen took a career-high 40 sacks during the regular season, that superpower faded. For all intents and purposes, the line of demarcation for pressure-to-sack rate is 20% in the NFL. item.title: 5 Players Withdraw From The ATP Lyon Open
item.description: Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 6, 2026 Frances Tiafoe of the U.S. in action during his round of 16 match against Russia's Daniil Medvedev IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Geoff Burke TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Steen Kirby The 2026 Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes Lyon, also knows as the Lyon Open, has suffered several withdrawals ahead of its October start. Injuries and scheduling decisions have affected the draw. Injuries have forced some players out of the ATP 250 event, while reasons behind other withdrawals remain unclear. The changes have also opened up places in the main draw for several replacements. 5 Players Withdraw From The ATP Lyon Open Which Players Withdrew from Lyon? Frances Tiafoe is among the most notable players to withdraw from the Lyon Open. The American pulled out after suffering a leg injury, and will be unable to play as he deals with his physical issue. Arthur Rinderknech has also withdrawn after suffering an abdominal injury. The Frenchman will be unable to compete in front of his home crowd. Arthur Géa has also withdrawn from the tournament. The Frenchman, who was competing in Shanghai, suffered a sharp psoas and right hip injury during his morning warmup before his quarterfinal match against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina . He attempted to play, but later retired during the first set. Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 7, 2026 France’s Arthur Gea in action during his round of 16 match against Netherlands’ Botic van de Zandschulp IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Geoff Burke Hubert Hurkacz and Denis Shapovalov have also withdrawn from the tournament. However, the reasons behind their decisions have not been publicly confirmed. Who Will Replace Those Players? Daniel Altmaier has been brought up to replace Frances Tiafoe. The German will face Titouan Droguet in the first round as he looks to make the most of his opportunity in Lyon. Benjamin Bonzi will replace Arthur Rinderknech in the draw. The Frenchman is set to open his campaign against Cameron Norrie. Meanwhile, Serbian player Hamad Medjedovic has been listed as Géa’s replacement and is set to face Brandon Nakashima in his opening match. Corentin Moutet and Jaime Faria have respectively been listed as replacements for Hurkacz and Shapovalov. Moutet will play against countryman Ugo Humbert in an all-French-first-round encounter, while Faria is schedule to play Felix Balshaw. With the tournament set to begin on October 19 , the withdrawals have brought several changes to the Lyon Open entry list. While injures account for some of the absences, the attention will now turn to the remaining players as they prepare for the start of the tournament. item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images ESPN and the College Football Playoff have reached a “handshake agreement” on a new 24-team format for next season. All told, ESPN is reportedly set to pay an additional $345 million for the expanded playoff, which represents about a 26% increase over the $1.3 billion per year it already paid for a 12-team format. Given that ESPN is doubling the playoff inventory it will own, paying just a 26% premium for the new inventory says a lot about how the network values these additional early-round games between schools in the back half of the top-25. That $345 million isn’t entirely new revenue, however. To secure that extra money, college football leadership agreed to eliminate conference championship games, which were revenue drivers themselves. Estimates peg the 10 conference championship games at $200 million to $300 million each year, with most of that revenue coming from the Power 4. According to reports, ESPN will receive a $140 million rebate from the conferences for the conference championship games it will no longer get to air. That brings ESPN’s total additional outlay for the expanded playoff down to $205 million. Additionally, Fox will receive about a $50 million rebate from the Big Ten for the cancellation of its conference championship game. item.title: Lions still ironing out plans for Brian Branch, Cade Mays vs. Packers
item.description: ALLEN PARK — Barring anything unforeseen, the Detroit Lions still plan on having defensive back Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) make their season debuts against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, Oct. 25. item.title: Michigan State Spartans Basketball Ranked #6 In Preseason Polls
item.description: Michigan State’s head coach Tom Izzo, right, talks with Coen Carr during the second half in the game against Incarnate Word on Friday, Oct. 2, 2026, at the Breslin Center in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The preseason basketball polls came out today, and to no surprise, our Michigan State Spartans are close to the top of the list. In both the AP and Coaches Polls, MSU opens the season as the sixth-ranked team. There has been hype all offseason about this team so the high ranking certainly feels warranted. Coming in at #1 in both polls are the Florida Gators. They are followed by the Duke Blue Devils at 2 and the Illinois Fighting Illini at 3. The AP Poll has UConn at 4 and Arizona at 5, while the Coaches Poll has those two flip-flopped. After MSU at 6, both polls have Texas at 7, and then they have Tennessee, Virginia, and Houston in varying orders. With Duke, Illinois, and Tennessee on our schedule this year, MSU will be facing three preseason top 10 squads. We also have an exhibition against UConn tomorrow evening. The other Big Ten teams appearing in preseason rankings are um (#16 AP/#20 Coaches), USC (21/22), UCLA (22 AP), and Purdue (24 Coaches). Featuring Jeremy Fears Jr. (a strong early candidate for Player of the Year honors), Coen Carr (the best athlete in college basketball), a number of returning players looking to take the next steps in their development, one of the best incoming freshmen classes in the country, and also Anton Bonke (the tallest Spartan ever), this team should have a little bit of everything (and a lot of somethings), to go toe-to-toe with any other team in the nation. We can start counting down the days until our season begins. Just 14 more days!

item.title: Kickoff time announced for Arizona football’s trip to Texas Tech
item.description: TUCSON, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 05: Quarterback Noah Fifita #11 of the Arizona Wildcats scrambles with the football against the Texas Tech Red Raiders during the second half of the NCAAF game at Arizona Stadium on October 05, 2024 in Tucson, Arizona. The Red Raiders defeated the Wildcats 28-22. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona still has to take care of business this weekend, but if things go as planned it could find itself getting plenty of national attention to end the month. The Wildcats’ Oct. 31 game at Texas Tech will kick off at 9 a.m. PT, with either ABC or and ESPN network airing the contest. That determination will be made after Saturday’s games, and it could mean ESPN’s College GameDay might be set to visit Lubbock and highlight the matchup. Arizona (5-1, 2-1 Big 12) is back in the national rankings at No. 25, while Tech is No. 8 and one of six unbeaten teams left in the country. The UA was supposed to play at Texas Tech in 2020, the return game of a home-and-home series that saw the Wildcats win at home in 2019, but COVID wiped out nonconference games. The Red Raiders beat Arizona 28-22 in 2024 and hold a 27-5-1 advantage in the all-time series which dates back to when the teams were in the Border Conference together. This will be Arizona’s first game at Tech since 1989. The UA is a victory away from being bowl eligible for the second year in a row, which last happened in 2014-15. It can lock up bowl eligibility with Saturday afternoon’s Homecoming game against Iowa State.

item.title: Villanova goes unranked in first AP Poll
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - MARCH 12: Villanova Wildcats head coach Kevin Willard during the first half of a Big East Men's Tournament Quarterfinal game against the Georgetown Hoyas at Madison Square Garden on March 12, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Porter Binks/Getty Images) There were two Big East teams selected in the initial top 25 of the AP Poll, and Villanova was not one of those teams. Connecticut was selected fourth, while St. John’s was picked 13th by the writers. Villanova received six votes, which essentially has the 38th in the rankings. Marquette was the only other Big East team to receive any votes (3). Villanova’s omission from the top 25 isn’t overly surprising, but seeing them behind schools like VCU, Saint Louis, Virginia Tech, etc. is. The talent that the Wildcats have on the roster is noticeably greater than those schools. The gap between votes for Villanova and schools such as Auburn, Nevada, Grand Canyon and Santa Clara is far too small, as well. All of this said, none of this really matters. Especially with the limbo for numerous teams on this list regarding fifth-year eligible players. The Wildcats will have a chance to show how good they are early in the season, as will the Big East as a whole. That will go a long way in establishing an AP Ranking throughout the season. The first opportunity comes in the exhibition game on Thursday, when Villanova faces no. 9 Virginia at the Finneran Pavilion. item.title: Charley Hull thinks three-time PGA Tour winner will become world number one, ‘that’s how high I rate him’
item.description: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Charley Hull believes that Michael Brennan has the talent to be the world number one in the future, as she explained why she rates the American so highly. Brennan is one of a number of extremely bright prospects making their way on the PGA Tour right now. The 26-year-old has already won three times, with his maiden victory last year enabling him to skip the Korn Ferry Tour and become a member at the game’s top table. Most recently, Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic in Japan. He is certainly going to be one name to watch out for in 2027, particularly with a Ryder Cup on the horizon. Interestingly, Charley Hull believes that Brennan is destined for the very top of the game. Charley Hull backs Michael Brennan to become world number one Right now, it is hard to imagine anyone being able to catch Scottie Scheffler at the top of the world rankings, with the 30-year-old proving to be the game’s most dominant player since Tiger Woods . But speaking to Golfweek , Hull suggested that it seems inevitable to her that Brennan will win one of the game’s four biggest events. “I was meant to be partners with Michael Brennan this year again in the Grant Thornton, but I can’t because I’m a bridesmaid at my best friend’s wedding, Georgia Hall, who plays on tour. I was pretty p—-d off with Georgia for not picking another date. Michael’s having a great season. If I could play with anyone on the PGA Tour, it would be Michael because he is one of the most impressive golfers I’ve ever seen and he’s going to be a major winner,” she said. Why Charley Hull was so impressed by Michael Brennan after they played in the same event Jacob Bridgeman claimed Brennan has the best swing on the PGA Tour after he had won at Yokohama Golf Club earlier this month. But it was Brennan’s personality that made a big impression on Hull last year, when they teamed up for the Grant Thornton Invitational. “I was meant to play with Daniel Berger last year and then he pulled out. Michael was first reserve. He’s such a nice guy. I had my niece out there with me and he couldn’t have treated her any better. I think he’s great for the game of golf. So, yeah, I see him definitely being a future world number one. Yeah, that’s how high I rate him, his golf game,” she added. Brennan certainly has the tools to thrive in the current game. He is third on tour for both strokes gained off the tee and driving distance during the 2026 season. He is also inside the top 75 for approach play and putting. The next challenge for Brennan will be winning one of the elevated events and contending in the majors. He made the cut at all four majors in 2026 without finishing inside the top-20. Hull is clearly confident that it will not be too long before Brennan is in the mix to win on the biggest stages.

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first versus third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ,” the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Vijay Singh, 63, Wasn’t Sure He Could Golf Because His Back Hurt. Then He Became the Second-Oldest Player to Win on the PGA Tour Champions
item.description: Vijay Singh Credit: Raj Mehta/Getty NEED TO KNOW Vijay Singh just made golf history The 63-year-old golfer became the second oldest to win a tournament on the PGA Tour Champions Singh won the SAS Championship by two strokes over Ernie Els Vijay Singh battled the cold — and an aching back — for a historic golf win! The PGA Tour Champions golfer became the second-oldest player to win on the circuit at age 63 following a two-shot victory at the SAS Championship on Sunday, Oct. 18. “This was a big one,” Singh said after closing out the tournament in Cary, N.C., with a 9-under total. “It’s been a tough year, all year, and then I didn’t know how I was going to play this morning. My back doesn’t do very well in cold. I didn’t hit my irons as good as I wanted to, but I got the job done.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! The only other golfer older than Singh to win a tournament on the 50-and-older circuit is Bernhard Langer, who won at the age of 67 in 2024 at the Charles Schwab Cup Championship at Phoenix Country Club. Vijay Singh Credit: Raj Mehta/Getty Singh has won 34 times on the PGA Tour, but Sunday marked only his sixth win on the senior tour, according to the Golf Channel . His last win was during the Ally Challenge in August 2023. The win was the Fijian golfer’s first top-10 finish this year. Amid a crowded leaderboard, the golfer made four birdies in a six-hole stretch as the field around him faltered. His six straight pars were enough to beat Ernie Els, who finished the tournament at 7-under. The tournament’s defending champion, Alex Cejka, and Tag Ridings tied for third at 6-under, three strokes back. For Singh, the win was proof that practice pays off. “This one feels good right now,” he said . “Hopefully it’s going to boost me up for the next few events to come and for next year. I think I kind of rededicated myself a little bit. I have been very lazy practicing.” He added, “I’ve been working out, but I haven’t been practicing very much. So I think I have to start doing that, which I started doing that again and I think that’s why I won today, I guess. Just the extra work that got me through.” Read the original article on People

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
